I reviewed all of lines 1–66 and the related declarations. Those were `RingAut` (an `abbrev` for `RingEquiv R R`, in Ring/Aut.lean), `MulSemiringAction.toRingEquiv` (`@[simps!]`, in Ring/Action/Group.lean), `RingHom.smul_def` (simp, in Ring/Action/Basic.lean), and `MulAut.smul_def` and `MulDistribMulAction.toMulAut` (in Group/Action/End.lean).

- **`RingAut.smul_def`:** It is `@[simp]` and rewrites `f • r` to `f r`. That matches the sibling lemmas `RingHom.smul_def`, `Function.End.smul_def` and `MulAut.smul_def`. It is the right direction and cannot loop.
- **`@[simps]` on `toRingAut`:** The generated lemma unfolds `toRingAut G R g` to `toRingEquiv G R g`. The `@[simps!]` lemma on `toRingEquiv` then gives `g • r`. This mirrors `MulDistribMulAction.toMulAut`. I found no competing rules, unwanted expansion or cycle.
- **Duplicate instance:** Ring/Action/Group.lean also declares `MulSemiringAction (R ≃+* R) R`, and `RingAut` is an abbreviation, so the two instances overlap. I think `smul_def` still fires, because both instances are defined with `smul := (· ·)`. I could not run Lean to check this. The overlap is not a clear simp-interface defect, so I did not report it.
